title: Cherry Creek
name: Cherry Creek
metaTitle: Cherry Creek 1031 Exchange Services | 1031 Exchange Denver
metaDescription: Cherry Creek 1031 exchange guidance for luxury retail, boutique office-over-retail, and high-basis mixed-use property in Denver's Cherry Creek North district.

sections.html: Cherry Creek is two things wearing one name: the enclosed Cherry Creek Shopping Center mall on the south side of First Avenue, and Cherry Creek North, the grid of boutique retail blocks on the other side of the street. Both sit a short drive from downtown Denver, and both carry some of the highest land values in the metro.

sections.heading: A Mall on One Side, a Village on the Other
sections.html:
Cherry Creek Shopping Center is anchor-driven, department stores and national retailers under one roof, and it trades like a regional mall asset with all the co-tenancy clauses and reciprocal easement agreements that come with that kind of ownership structure. Cherry Creek North is the opposite, small two- and three-story buildings, ground-floor boutique retail with office or residential above, laid out on a walkable street grid rather than around a parking structure.

A buyer needs to know which side of First Avenue a parcel sits on before running comps, because the lease structures, tenant mix, and buyer pool are not interchangeable between the two.

The office space that does exist in Cherry Creek North skews small and boutique, wealth managers, law firms, and design studios taking a floor or two above a retail storefront rather than a corporate tenant leasing an entire building. That tenant profile leases and renews differently than a DTC corporate campus, smaller suites, shorter negotiation cycles, and less sensitivity to parking ratio since most of these tenants and their clients arrive on foot or by rideshare.

sections.heading: What Trades in This Submarket
sections.html:
Realistic replacement property in Cherry Creek looks like:

  • boutique retail storefronts in Cherry Creek North with office or residential above
  • small multi-tenant retail buildings fronting First Avenue or Second Avenue
  • mall-adjacent pad sites and outparcels near the shopping center
  • high-end condo or apartment buildings with ground-floor commercial space

sections.heading: Land Basis and What It Means for Underwriting
sections.html:
Cherry Creek land trades at a premium to almost anywhere else on this identification list outside of a handful of downtown parcels. That premium shows up as a lower going-in cap rate, and a buyer underwriting on cap rate alone will pass on Cherry Creek every time. The case here is usually rent growth and redevelopment optionality on an underbuilt lot, not current yield.

The Cherry Creek Trail runs along the south edge of the district and adds foot and bike traffic that supports the boutique retail rents in Cherry Creek North better than the trail alone would suggest on paper. That amenity value is real but hard to put a number on, so don't let a broker's pro forma lean on it too hard.

sections.heading: Diligence Specific to This District
sections.html:
Confirm reciprocal easement and co-tenancy language on anything tied to the mall, since a large anchor's lease terms can affect smaller in-line tenants around it. On Cherry Creek North buildings, check parking, most rely on shared or metered street parking rather than dedicated lots, and that constraint has killed more than one tenant's expansion plan before it started.

The annual Cherry Creek Arts Festival closes several blocks of Cherry Creek North to vehicle traffic every summer, and ground-floor retailers on the closure route see a real, if temporary, jump in foot traffic and pop-up vendor competition. Any lease review for a Cherry Creek North storefront should check whether the tenant has a co-tenancy or percentage-rent clause tied to that event, since it can swing a single month's numbers meaningfully.

sections.heading: Positioning a Cherry Creek Identification
sections.html: Given the high entry basis, Cherry Creek property usually anchors an identification list rather than filling out the back end of one. Investors coordinating a 1031 into this submarket often pair it with a lower-basis DTC office asset or a Denver Tech Center building to balance the exchange's overall cash flow, since Cherry Creek's return profile leans more on appreciation than on day-one yield. A qualified intermediary should also confirm early how any anchor lease renewal or co-tenancy trigger tied to the shopping center could affect a nearby Cherry Creek North parcel's value, since a large anchor's lease decision can ripple into rent expectations for smaller buildings blocks away.

faqs.q: Why does Cherry Creek trade at a lower cap rate than the rest of the Denver metro?
faqs.a: Land basis. Cherry Creek carries some of the highest per-square-foot land values in the metro, and buyers are generally paying for rent growth and redevelopment upside rather than current yield.

faqs.q: Is Cherry Creek Shopping Center itself a realistic 1031 replacement asset?
faqs.a: Only for a well-capitalized buyer. It's an institutional-scale mall asset with co-tenancy and reciprocal easement obligations that most exchange buyers are better matched to a smaller Cherry Creek North storefront or outparcel instead.

faqs.q: How much does parking limit Cherry Creek North retail?
faqs.a: It's a real constraint. Most buildings depend on shared or metered street parking rather than dedicated off-street spaces, and that has stalled tenant expansion plans more than once.

faqs.q: Does the Cherry Creek Trail actually add value to nearby retail?
faqs.a: It supports foot traffic and rents in Cherry Creek North, but that value is hard to quantify precisely, so don't let a seller's pro forma treat it as a guaranteed rent premium.

faqs.q: How does Cherry Creek usually fit into a three-property identification?
faqs.a: It typically anchors the list given its high entry price, paired with a lower-basis DTC or Denver Tech Center asset to balance the overall exchange's cash flow.
